column2: post-apply vendor rows can fall outside the per-round gantt window because round end is recorded before `_step5_post_round_gates`. `record_round_timing` runs immediately after `_run_round` returns, but `_step5_post_round_gates` (the only caller of post-apply `run_relevant_checks` / `run_lint_fix`) runs later on the `fix-applied` branch. new `claude-relevant-checks` / `claude-lint-fix` rows will have `start_s` after that recorded `end_s`. `_progress_vendor_rows` clips to the round `gantt_window` from `v1 round` rows, so the new bars may never render and the reported blank gaps can remain.

an outer `run_lint_fix` timing wrapper overlaps existing agent-launcher vendor rows and conflicts with the plan's single-envelope-bar goal. `launch_claude_lint_fix_main` already records `task_kind` `claude-lint-fix` when checks `_run_claude` succeeds; wrapping all of `run_lint_fix` adds a second `claude-lint-fix` bar for the same claude invocation (with partial overlap on codex/cursor waterfall attempts). codex lint-fix already records `codex-exec` via `launch-codex-exec`, so an outer `claude-lint-fix` wrapper stacks atop that on codex success. the result is duplicate/overlapping gantt bars that misstate where wall-clock time went and inflate attributed duration.

planned `.log` output basenames will not render as clean `claude/...` labels. `_progress_core_from_output()` strips only `.txt` and `-output`, so the new timing rows will display as `claude/relevant-checks.log` and `claude/lint-fix.log` instead of the intended clean labels.

the planned `run_lint_fix` wrapper omits the `start_s` capture and `try`/`finally` envelope that `run_relevant_checks` specifies and that failure modes require for exception paths. the refactor bullets jump from "keep signature unchanged" to "call `_run_lint_fix_impl`" and a `finally` that reads `outcome.coder_tool`, without initializing `outcome`, without `start_s = int(time.time())`, and without a `try` around the impl call. an exception after work begins (for example under `run_dir` setup or git probes) can leave a long unlabeled gantt interval, the same defect class as the bug report. mirror the `run_relevant_checks` wrapper: set `outcome = none`, capture `start_s`, wrap `_run_lint_fix_impl` in `try`/`finally`, and in `finally` record when a timing root exists, `outcome is not none`, and `outcome.coder_tool != "claude"` (use exit code 1 and `status complete` on exceptions).

the plan defers round `end_s` until after `_step5_post_round_gates`, but step 5 also uses `gate_continue=true` (bulk skip-ratio and substantial-change continuations). if `record_round_timing` is added only on terminal fix-applied exits, or is placed after the `if gate_continue: continue` branch, intermediate fix-applied rounds never get a post-gate round row and later gantt windows can still clip or omit post-apply vendor bars.

deferred round timing is only scheduled after `_step5_post_round_gates` returns. today `record_round_timing` runs before the status branch, so a fix-applied round always gets a round row even when `_step5_post_round_gates` raises. the plan skips the early call and records only after gates return. if `run_lint_fix` re-raises after its `finally` timing row, or any other gate path raises, the deferred call never runs and the round loses its timing window while vendor rows may already exist.

the planned `run_relevant_checks` wrapper is internally inconsistent and weaker than the `run_lint_fix` pattern it claims to mirror. the plan uses `finally` and `outcome exists` but does not require `try` / `finally`, `outcome = none`, or assigning `outcome = _run_relevant_checks_impl(...)` inside `try`. it also mixes `result.exit_code` with `outcome`. a literal `return _run_relevant_checks_impl(...)` inside `try` leaves `outcome` unset, so the `finally` guard never fires and successful step 5 post-apply checks still produce no `claude-relevant-checks` bar.

the planned private timing helper does not take or route through the existing `runner` passed into `run_relevant_checks` / `run_lint_fix`, unlike `_mark_step_ledger`. the helper spec only describes invoking `python/cli.py timing record-vendor-task` via env vars (or shelling out directly, as `_record_coder_vendor_task` does in `review_and_fix.py`). planned `test_checks.py` assertions require `stubrunner.calls` on `timing record-vendor-task`. a subprocess-only helper would pass runtime but fail mandated tests, diverge from the established `checks.py` pattern, and force extra monkeypatching to observe recording.

the `run_lint_fix` refactor bullets still omit explicit `outcome = none`, `start_s` capture, and `return outcome` even though `run_relevant_checks` lists them and failure modes require the full envelope. `run_relevant_checks` bullets require both initializations; `run_lint_fix` bullets jump straight to try/finally without them. a literal implementer following only the lint-fix subsection can hit `unboundlocalerror` in `finally` on exceptions, emit rows with missing/wrong `start_s`, leave exception paths unlabeled, or return inside `try` without proper `--start-s`/`--end-s` on success—recreating the silent-gap bug class on lint-fix exception paths.
